Why this range: Inverse regularisation strength, on a log scale. 0.001 = very strong L2 shrinkage (underfitting risk), 100 = almost none. Only 6 values, so every one is tried (grid search).
Main complexity control: a tree of depth d can encode interactions of up to d features. 1 is a single split, 10 is deep enough to memorise the training set, so the search brackets the useful range.
Forbids leaves built on a handful of rows. Each label comes from only 100 replicates, so tiny leaves would fit noise. 5 to 19 is the zone where a default tree stops memorising.
Number of features examined at each split: all (None), sqrt or log2 of the number of features. Fewer features add randomness and can reduce variance.
Impurity measure for the splits. Gini and entropy usually give similar trees, both are tried.
Cost-complexity pruning strength, from 0 (no pruning) to 0.01 (aggressive). Pruning removes branches that add little, which also makes the tree easier to read.
Number of trees. Averaging more trees lowers the variance with diminishing returns; 50 to 300 covers the plateau at a reasonable cost.
Capped at 6 on purpose: a default forest memorised the training set. Shallow trees act as weak learners, which suits averaging. If the chosen value is 6, the cap is binding.
Minimum samples needed to split a node. Larger values force coarser, more stable splits.
Minimum samples per leaf. Prevents leaves built on a handful of noisy labels.
Share of features tried at each split (sqrt and log2 of 9 features = 3, 0.5 = 4 or 5). Fewer features decorrelate the trees.
Number of boosting rounds. With a small learning rate many rounds are needed; 300 to 1000 covers the useful range.
Depth of each tree = the order of interactions it can capture. Capped at 6 to limit overfitting.
Step-size shrinkage. Small values (0.01 to 0.03) make each tree contribute little, which regularises. They need many rounds.
Share of the rows used by each tree (50 to 70%): stochastic boosting, which reduces overfitting.
Share of the features used by each tree (50 to 70%): decorrelates the trees.
Minimum total weight needed in a leaf. High values (10, 11, 12) forbid leaves built on a few noisy labels.
L1 penalty on the leaf weights (0 = none). Encourages sparse, smaller leaf values.
L2 penalty on the leaf weights (0 = none). Smooths the leaf values.
Architecture, from one layer of 32 neurons to three layers (128, 128 or 64, 64, 32). Wide enough to model interactions between nine inputs without hand-limiting the capacity.
ReLU (default, fast) versus tanh (smooth, often better on small tabular data).
L2 penalty on the weights, on a log scale from almost none (1e-6) to strong (0.1). Controls overfitting together with early stopping.
Initial step of Adam, on a log-like scale. Too small learns slowly, too large is unstable.
Mini-batch size. Smaller batches add noise that can help generalisation; larger ones are more stable.
Maximum number of epochs. Early stopping normally ends training before this limit.
